comments.title: Transformer Pad Clearance Dimensions Missing from Electrical Plans
comments.comment: All four transformer pads on the electrical site plan lack dimensioned clearances to adjacent buildings, parking areas, sidewalks, and other site features.
comments.issue:
UCM § 1.10.4 Table 1.10.4 mandates specific dimensioned clearances from pad-mounted transformers to all adjacent features, but no clearance dimensions or annotations appear on Sheet 21 or Sheet 9 for any of the four transformer pads. The following specific clearance requirements are unverifiable:
- Building-to-pad clearances: 10 ft on hot-stick/door side, 15 ft if facing a confined space/niche, 5 ft on operator/control sides, 3 ft on other sides adjacent to brick/masonry 2-hour fire-rated buildings, greater clearances for non-brick/masonry buildings
- Adjacent building construction type (brick/masonry with 2-hour fire rating vs. non-brick/masonry) is not documented — required to determine which clearance column in Table 1.10.4 applies; AE Design written approval is required if reduced clearances are used per UCM § 1.10.4 footnote 2
- Window and door clearances: 5 ft lateral, or 12 ft vertical if lateral clearance is less than 5 ft
- Oil-filled equipment to fire escapes/stairs: 20 ft minimum horizontal/radial clearance
- Transformer pad to back of sidewalk: 2 ft minimum; visual analysis indicates T1, T2, and T4 appear to be at or within 2 ft of adjacent sidewalks, but no dimensions confirm compliance
comments.sheets: Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21); Site Plan (Sheet 9)
comments.applicableArea: All four transformer pad locations: west of Building 1 (near Unit 101), between Buildings 2 and 8, between Buildings 4 and 5, between Buildings 6 and 7 (near Unit 705); adjacent buildings, driveways, parking areas, sidewalks, and pedestrian paths throughout the site
comments.resolution: Add clearance dimension annotations to Sheet 21 and Sheet 9 for all four transformer pads showing measured distances to: adjacent buildings on all sides, parking areas, driveways, back of sidewalk, windows and doors, and fire escapes/stairs. Document adjacent building construction type (brick/masonry with 2-hour fire rating vs. non-brick/masonry) for each building adjacent to a transformer pad to identify the applicable clearance column. Confirm all dimensions meet Table 1.10.4 minimums (10 ft hot-stick side, 15 ft facing confined space, 20 ft oil-filled equipment to fire escapes/stairs, 5 ft operator sides, 2 ft from back of sidewalk); if any clearance is reduced below the standard, provide AE Design written approval per UCM § 1.10.4 footnote 2.

perRunFindings.comment: Provide dimensioned clearances from all four transformer pads to adjacent buildings, parking areas, driveways, and structures per UCM § 1.10.4 requirements (10 feet for hot-stick use area, 5 feet for sides with operators/controls, 3-5 feet for other sides depending on building construction type). Confirm building construction types if any clearances are less than standard requirements.
applicableAreas: Four transformer pad locations on the site
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) identifies four locations labeled 'Electrical Transformer Pad': (1) west of Building 1 near Unit 101, (2) west of Building 8 near Unit 801, (3) south of Building 5 near Unit 504, and (4) north of Building 7 near Unit 705. All four pads are shown as simple squares with no dimension lines showing clearances to adjacent buildings, parking areas, walkways, or structures. The site plan shows driveways and parking areas in close proximity to these pads, but no distances are dimensioned.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 Table 1.10.4 specifies clearance requirements for pad-mounted equipment based on the type of adjacent structures and whether the equipment has operator/control access. Required clearances range from 3 feet (non-operator sides, non-brick/masonry buildings) to 10 feet (hot-stick use area). The absence of dimensioned clearances prevents verification that the design complies with these minimum setbacks and prevents determination of whether reduced clearances (3 feet instead of 5 feet) require AE Design written approval per UCM § 1.10.4 footnote 2. Building construction type (brick/masonry with 2-hour fire rating vs. non-brick/masonry) must be documented to determine which clearance column in Table 1.10.4 applies.

perRunFindings.comment: Clearances from the four transformer pads are not shown or dimensioned on any plan sheets. Design must provide UCM § 1.10.4 compliant clearances (10 ft hot-stick area, 5 ft operator areas, 3 ft other sides) dimensioned from each pad to buildings, parking, driveways, and other obstructions. Building construction type (brick/masonry 2-hour fire-rated vs. non-brick/masonry) must be documented to determine applicable clearance table.
applicableAreas: Transformer pad locations near Buildings 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, and 8; near parking areas and driveways
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows four transformer pads with generic labels only ('Electrical Transformer Pad') and no specifications (kVA ratings, dimensions, or type). Sheet 9 (Site Plan) displays the same transformer locations in spatial context with buildings, driveways, parking spaces, and sidewalks. Vision analysis of Sheet 21 confirmed that no clearance dimensions or lines are dimensioned from any transformer pad to nearby buildings, parking areas, driveways, or sidewalks. The drawing shows relationships graphically but provides zero quantitative clearance verification.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 Table 1.10.4 specifies clearance requirements from pad-mounted equipment: minimum 10 feet on hot-stick use area (side with door), 5 feet on sides with operators/controls, and 3 feet on sides without operators/controls (from removable ventilated obstructions). Additionally, buildings affect these clearances — non-brick/masonry buildings trigger the standard clearances; brick/masonry with 2-hour fire rating allows reduced clearances. No building construction types are documented, and no clearance dimensions are shown from the transformers to any adjacent structures. The plans cannot demonstrate compliance with Table 1.10.4 without these dimensions and without knowledge of building construction type.

perRunFindings.comment: Transformer pad clearances from buildings, parking areas, sidewalks, and other structures not shown or dimensioned on electrical design plan. Provide dimensioned clearance details for both transformer pads per UCM § 1.10.4 Table 1.10.4 (minimum 3 feet to 10 feet depending on side and building type), including verification of building construction type (brick/masonry with 2-hour fire rating vs. non-brick/masonry) for clearance determination.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) depicts two transformer pads on the site plan drawing. The vision analysis of Sheet 21 confirmed that no dimensions or clearance radii are labeled for either transformer pad. The pads are drawn in proximity to parking areas, driveways, and building footprints, but no specific clearance distances are dimensioned or noted. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows the overall layout with buildings and parking areas but provides no transformer pad clearance dimensions. The preliminary electrical plan shows the general locations of the two transformer pads but provides no evidence of compliance with the minimum clearance requirements specified in UCM § 1.10.4 Table 1.10.4 (10 ft hot-stick use area, 5 ft sides with operators/controls, 3 ft other sides based on building type and fire rating).
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 requires specific clearances from pad-mounted equipment based on the side of the equipment and building construction type. The required clearances range from 3 feet to 10 feet depending on the side and building characteristics. The applicant's burden is to demonstrate compliance through dimensioned drawings. The absence of any clearance dimensions or notes on the electrical plan and site plan means the requirement cannot be verified. The deficiency is not that compliance might not exist in reality, but that the required documentation is absent.

perRunFindings.comment: Transformer pad locations shown on Sheet 21 do not include dimensioned clearances to adjacent buildings, parking areas, sidewalks, or other features. Add dimensions to all transformer pads showing clearances to: adjacent buildings (minimum 10-15 feet per UCM § 1.10.4), parking/traffic areas (maximum 6 feet, with bollards if less than 4 feet), windows and doors (minimum 5-12 feet per orientation), and fire escapes/stairs (minimum 20 feet if oil-filled equipment). Verify all clearances meet Table 1.10.4 requirements.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) depicts three electrical transformer pads: one west of Building 2/northwest of Building 8 near the western property line and street entrance; one between Buildings 8 and 6 in the central driveway/alley area; and one east of Building 5 near the eastern property boundary. The vision analysis confirmed: 'There are no specific dimensions (e.g., distance lines with measurements) provided on this sheet to indicate the exact clearances from the transformer pads to the buildings, doors, or windows.' No clearance dimensions are shown from any transformer pad to: adjacent buildings (Buildings 2, 5, 6, 8), building doors or windows, parking areas, sidewalks, or fire escapes.
perRunFindings.reasoning: EL-19.27 specifies 'Proposed buildings, bike racks, or site features do not meet required safety clearances from Austin Energy facilities' and applies 'Only when site is adjacent to Austin Energy facilities requiring safety clearances.' UCM § 1.10.4 establishes specific minimum clearances from pad-mounted transformers and distribution equipment based on configuration and adjacent features.

perRunFindings.comment: Add clearance dimensions to the electrical site plan for each of the four transformer pad locations per UCM § 1.10.4 Table 1.10.4. For each pad, dimension the clearances to: adjacent buildings, parking areas, driveways, pedestrian walkways, fencing, mail kiosks, and any other site features. Specify clearances in feet (minimum 5-20 feet depending on configuration). Indicate bollard locations if pads are within 4 feet of parking or traffic areas. Specify sidewalk setback (minimum 2 feet from back of sidewalk) and truck access route (minimum 6 feet adjacent clearance). Add notes confirming compliance with UCM § 1.10.4 clearance requirements.
applicableAreas: Transformer pads and clearances to buildings, parking, and site features
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows four transformer pad locations: (1) northwest corner near Building 1, (2) between Buildings 2 and 8, (3) between Buildings 4 and 5, and (4) between Buildings 6 and 7. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) depicts these transformer pads in relation to buildings and parking areas. However, visual analysis of Sheet 21 found 'absolutely no dimensions, dashed clearance lines, or safety zones drawn or annotated around any of this equipment.' Similarly, analysis of Sheet 9 found 'no explicit clearance or setback dimensions shown between the Transformer Pad and the adjacent buildings, parking areas, or other site features.'
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 Table 1.10.4 establishes mandatory minimum clearances from pad-mounted transformers: (1) Hot-stick use area to adjacent building/structure: minimum 10 feet; (2) Hot-stick use area facing confined space: minimum 15 feet; (3) Oil-filled equipment to fire escape/stairs: minimum 20 feet; (4) Adjacent to brick/masonry building (2-hour fire rating): minimum 5 feet from side edges; (5) Adjacent to non-brick/masonry building: minimum 12 feet from oil-filled equipment; (6) Windows, doors, ventilating ducts: 5 feet lateral or 12 feet vertical if lateral less than 5 feet; (7) Equipment pads within 6 feet from parking/traffic areas must have truck access, and bollards required if within 4 feet; (8) Transformer pads must be 2 feet from back of sidewalks.

perRunFindings.comment: Multiple transformer pads appear to be located within 2 feet of concrete sidewalks per visual analysis of Sheet 9. Provide: (1) Updated site plan with dimension lines and callouts clearly documenting the distance from back of sidewalk to each transformer pad (T1, T2, T3, T4), confirming minimum 2-foot clearance per UCM § 1.10.4, OR (2) Reposition transformers to achieve minimum 2-foot separation from all sidewalks, or (3) If clearance cannot be achieved, provide documented approval from Austin Energy Design authorizing reduced sidewalk clearance with specific approval conditions.
applicableAreas: All four transformer pads (T1, T2, T3, T4) relative to adjacent sidewalks and pedestrian paths
perRunFindings.observation: Examined Sheet 9 (Site Plan) to measure distance from transformer pads to sidewalks and pedestrian paths. Vision analysis identified clearances for each transformer: 'T1: A Concrete Sidewalk wraps tightly around the eastern and northern sides of this pad. It appears to be within 2 feet of the pad. T2: A concrete sidewalk running north-south along the side of Bldg. 4 passes very close to the western edge of this pad (appears to be within 2 feet). T3: A concrete walkway runs east-west just north of the pad, connecting the driveway to Unit 604. It appears to be within 2 to 5 feet. T4: A concrete sidewalk runs north-south just to the east of the pad, leading to Unit 801. It appears to be within 2 feet.' Three of the four transformers (T1, T2, T4) are documented as being within 2 feet of sidewalks. No specific dimension lines, callouts, or clearance annotations are provided on the site plan.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 specifies: 'Transformer equipment pads not minimum 2 feet from back of sidewalks.' Vision analysis indicates T1, T2, and T4 are at or potentially less than the 2-foot minimum. The absence of specific dimension documentation on the site plan creates ambiguity.

perRunFindings.comment: Transformer equipment pads not minimum 2 feet from back of sidewalks. Sidewalk shown immediately adjacent to transformer pad without documented minimum clearance.
applicableAreas: Westernmost transformer pad location on western property line near Building 1
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows a concrete sidewalk labeled 'Construct 6\' Concrete Sidewalk' immediately to the west of the transformer pad marked 'Transformer Pad (Typ.)'. Vision analysis confirmed 'To the immediate west of the pad is a pathway labeled "Construct 6\' Concrete Sidewalk."' The exact distance between the transformer pad and the back of this sidewalk is not dimensioned on the plan. Visual estimation from the plan at scale 1" = 20' suggests the sidewalk is very close (potentially less than 2 feet) from the transformer pad.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 requires a minimum 2-foot clearance from transformer pads to the back of sidewalks. The site plan shows a sidewalk immediately adjacent to (west of) the transformer pad, but does not dimension the specific clearance.

perRunFindings.comment: Dimension the distance from each transformer pad to the back (furthest from street/building) of adjacent sidewalks to verify minimum 2-foot clearance per UCM § 1.10.4. If any pad is less than 2 feet from sidewalk, redesign pad location.
applicableAreas: Transformer pad locations near sidewalks and pedestrian paths
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows concrete sidewalks and decomposed granite walkways throughout the site near the buildings and around the detention pond. Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows transformer pad locations. However, there are no dimension lines or text specifying the clearance distances from any transformer pad to the adjacent sidewalks or pedestrian paths.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 requires that 'Equipment pads be located minimum 2 feet from back of sidewalks.' Without dimensioned drawings, the applicant has not demonstrated that this minimum 2-foot clearance is maintained at all transformer locations. Visual proximity does not constitute dimensional compliance verification.

comments.title: Bollard Protection Not Shown at Transformer Pads Near Parking and Drive Aisles
comments.comment: No bollard protection is shown at transformer pads positioned adjacent to drive aisles and surface parking areas.
comments.issue: UCM § 1.10.4 requires 4-inch minimum galvanized rigid metal post bollards per AE Design equipment pad standard details when pad-mounted equipment is within 4 feet of parking or traffic areas, sized to allow equipment door opening. Transformer 2 (between Buildings 4/5) is visually identified as within 2 feet of a surface parking space, and Transformer 3 (between Buildings 6/7) is positioned immediately adjacent to a paved drive aisle and surface parking — both well within the 4-foot trigger threshold. No bollards, protective barriers, or notations referencing bollard requirements appear on Sheet 21, Sheet 9, or any detail sheet for any of the four transformer pads. Without dimensioned pad-to-parking distances, compliance cannot be verified at any location.
comments.sheets: Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21); Site Plan (Sheet 9)
comments.applicableArea: All four transformer pad locations; particularly Transformer 2 (between Buildings 4/5, adjacent to surface parking) and Transformer 3 (between Buildings 6/7, adjacent to drive aisle and surface parking); western pads near Building 1 and Building 8 adjacent to internal drive aisles
comments.resolution: Dimension the distance from each transformer pad to the nearest parking stall edge and drive aisle curb on Sheet 21 and Sheet 9. For any transformer pad within 4 feet of a parking area or traffic lane, add 4-inch minimum galvanized rigid metal post bollards per AE Design equipment pad standard details, spaced to allow full equipment door opening, and show bollard locations on Sheet 21 and Sheet 9 with a reference to the standard detail. If all pads are confirmed to be more than 4 feet from all parking and traffic areas, add a note to that effect on the plan.

perRunFindings.comment: Transformer pad locations are shown on electrical design plan but distances to parking/traffic areas are not dimensioned. Bollard protection details are not shown. Verification required that all pads are either more than 4 feet from parking/traffic or that 4-inch minimum galvanized rigid metal post bollards are detailed per UCM § 1.10.4.
applicableAreas: transformer pad locations near parking areas
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design) shows 4 transformer pads located at: west side near entrance drive (landscape island), southwest area near entrance (landscape island), east side central area (between Bldg. 4 and 5), and southeast area (between Bldg. 6 and 7). Vision analysis of Sheet 21 indicated that 'None of the transformer pads appear to be within 4 feet of designated parking stalls' based on visual inspection, but the analysis noted the lack of explicit distance dimensions on the plan. Without precise distance measurements between the transformer pads and the nearest parking stalls/traffic areas, and without bollard details shown on the electrical plan, it cannot be definitively confirmed whether the 4-foot minimum clearance requirement is met at all locations.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 requires that pad-mounted equipment within 4 feet of parking or traffic areas must have 4-inch minimum galvanized rigid metal post bollards per AE Design equipment pad details. The site plan shows transformer locations and parking areas but does not provide dimensioned distances from pads to parking/traffic edges. The lack of explicit distance callouts and the absence of any bollard details on the electrical plan create ambiguity.

perRunFindings.comment: Bollards not shown when equipment pads are within 4 feet of parking/traffic areas. Add 4-inch minimum galvanized rigid metal bollards around each transformer pad per Austin Energy Design equipment pad details. Show bollard locations and spacing on site plan with reference to AE Design standard details.
applicableAreas: Middle areas adjacent to drive aisles
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 shows four transformer pads (dashed rectangles) at locations middle-left (west of Bldg 1), bottom-left (west of Bldg 8), middle-right (between Bldgs 4-5), and bottom-right (between Bldgs 6-7). Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows these transformer pads immediately adjacent to internal drive aisles (parking and traffic areas). No bollards, protective barriers, or any protective posts are shown around any of the transformer pad locations. No callouts or notes reference bollard requirements.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 requires 4-inch minimum galvanized rigid metal posts (bollards) per AE Design equipment pad details when pad-mounted equipment is within 4 feet of parking or traffic areas. The transformer pads shown on Sheet 9 are positioned directly adjacent to internal drive aisles and parking areas, placing them well within the 4-foot proximity threshold. The absence of bollards on all four transformer pads is a deficiency.

perRunFindings.comment: Transformer 3 is located within 4 feet of surface parking and drive aisle but no bollards are shown. Provide 4-inch minimum galvanized rigid metal bollard posts per AE Design equipment pad details, positioned to protect the transformer pad from vehicular impact and maintain required clearances.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 (Electrical Plan) depicts three transformer pads. Vision analysis of Sheet 9 (Site Plan) confirms that Transformer 3 (located between Buildings 6 and 7 on the east side of the site) is positioned within a paved area with surface parking spaces to the northwest and the main concrete drive aisle immediately adjacent. The transformer is clearly within 4 feet of parking and traffic circulation areas. Sheet 21 shows the transformer pad symbol but contains no indication of bollards, protective posts, or any barrier/protection device at this location. No detail sheet (Sheets 22-39) provides bollard details for this transformer location.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 requires 4-inch minimum galvanized rigid metal posts (bollards) per AE Design equipment pad details for pad-mounted equipment located within 4 feet of parking or traffic areas. Transformer 3 is clearly within 4 feet of surface parking spaces and a paved drive aisle. The absence of bollards shown on the electrical plan or detail sheets indicates this requirement has not been addressed.

perRunFindings.comment: Measure the distance from each transformer pad to the nearest parking/traffic area on Sheet 21. If any transformer is within 4 feet of parking/traffic areas, show bollard locations and spacing (sized to allow equipment door opening) on the Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21), Site Plan (Sheet 9), and Landscape Plan (Sheet 31). If all transformers are more than 4 feet from parking/traffic areas, note this on the plan.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 shows 5 transformer pads but does not display bollard symbols or callouts. The checklist item specifically applies 'only when pad-mounted transformer is within 4 feet of parking/traffic areas.' Transformers are not shown on the Site Plan (Sheet 9) or other discipline plans, making it impossible to accurately measure distances from transformer pads to the nearest parking or traffic areas using the plans.
perRunFindings.reasoning: This item is conditionally applicable only if any of the 5 transformers are located within 4 feet of parking or traffic areas. While Sheet 21 shows both transformers and parking areas, the distance relationship is not explicitly annotated with dimensions. To verify whether bollards are required, the distance from each transformer pad to the nearest parking/traffic area must be measured or explicitly noted on the plans.

perRunFindings.comment: Transformer pad 2 is positioned less than 2 feet from a surface parking space, triggering the bollard requirement per UCM § 1.10.4. No bollards are shown on the electrical or site plans. Provide: (1) Detail drawing for 4-inch minimum galvanized rigid metal bollards (per UCM § 1.10.4 standard specification) positioned around Transformer 2, with spacing adequate to allow equipment door openings and access (minimum 3-foot clear width for door swing), OR (2) Reposition Transformer 2 to a location more than 4 feet from all parking spaces and traffic areas.
applicableAreas: Transformer pad 2 (eastern location, between Bldg. 4 and 5, adjacent to parking)
perRunFindings.observation: Examined Sheets 21 and 9 to identify transformer pad locations and proximity to parking areas. Transformer 2 (eastern side, between Bldg. 4 and 5) is positioned immediately adjacent to a surface parking space with less than 2 feet of separation per vision analysis: 'T2 is located directly adjacent to a perpendicular surface parking space. It appears to share a boundary or sit mere inches from the northernmost parking space in the cluster west of Bldg. 5. It is absolutely within 6 feet of this parking space.' No bollard symbols or notations are shown on Sheet 21 or Sheet 9 at this transformer location.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 specifies: 'Bollard requirement when transformer pad is within 4 feet of parking/traffic areas... 4-inch minimum galvanized rigid metal bollards are required and must be spaced to allow equipment door opening.' Transformer 2 is less than 2 feet from a parking space, well within the 4-foot trigger distance.

perRunFindings.comment: Measure and show the distance from each transformer pad to the nearest parking/traffic area. If any pad is within 4 feet, show bollard locations and spacing (minimum 4-inch galvanized rigid metal posts) designed to allow equipment door opening.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows four transformer pad locations but does not indicate distances to adjacent parking or driveway areas, nor are any bollards shown. No dimensions are provided that would allow verification of whether transformer pads are within 4 feet of parking/traffic areas or outside this distance. Vision analysis confirms: 'There is no indication of dedicated electrical clearance zones, specific electrical maintenance access routes, or bollard locations protecting the electrical equipment.'
perRunFindings.reasoning: Per UCM § 1.10.4, when pad-mounted transformers are located within 4 feet of parking or traffic areas, 4-inch minimum galvanized rigid metal post bollards are required, spaced to allow equipment door opening. Bollards protect the equipment from vehicle damage. Without measuring distances from transformer pads to parking areas and showing required bollards, it cannot be verified that the site design protects equipment or meets code requirements.

comments.title: AE Truck Access Routes and Laydown Curb Requirements Not Documented
comments.comment: Plans do not dimension transformer pad distances to drivable surfaces or document Austin Energy truck access routes.
comments.issue: UCM § 1.10.4 requires transformer pads to be located within 6 feet of a parking or traffic area for Austin Energy truck accessibility; if any pad exceeds this distance, a dedicated access route with laydown curbs (minimum 12-foot width, adequate load capacity for transformer trucks) must be provided or written AE Design approval must be obtained. No plan sheet dimensions pad-to-drivable-surface distances, and no laydown curb specifications, access route details, or notes confirming 6-foot compliance are shown on Sheet 9, Sheet 11, or Sheet 21.
comments.sheets: Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21); Site Plan (Sheet 9); Grading Plan (Sheet 11)
comments.applicableArea: All four transformer pad locations relative to adjacent drive aisles and parking areas
comments.resolution: Add dimension annotations to Sheet 9 and Sheet 21 showing the distance from each transformer pad to the nearest drivable surface (drive aisle or parking area). If all pads are within 6 feet, add a note to that effect on the plan. If any pad exceeds 6 feet from a drivable surface, provide a dedicated access route design with laydown curb details (minimum 12-foot width, load capacity adequate for transformer truck loads) per UCM § 1.10.4, or submit written AE Design approval for an alternative access arrangement.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Low confidence (1–2/3 runs) — visual review suggests pads are within 6 feet of driveways but no plan dimensions confirm; reviewer should verify whether access routes and laydown curbs are adequate.

perRunFindings.comment: Dimension the distance from each transformer pad to the nearest parking area or traffic lane to verify compliance with UCM § 1.10.4 requirement that pads be within 6 feet of parking/traffic for AE truck accessibility. If distances exceed 6 feet, provide written Austin Energy Design approval for alternative spacing.
applicableAreas: Transformer pad locations relative to parking and traffic areas
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows 88 parking spaces (10 surface, 78 garage) and internal driveways. Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows four transformer pads: one west of Buildings 1/2 adjacent to a driveway curve, one between Buildings 4 and 5 near parking/circulation, one between Buildings 6 and 7 near parking/circulation, and one west of Building 8 near the property line. Vision analysis indicates that transformers appear to be in close proximity to parking and traffic areas, but 'there are absolutely no dimensions shown on this sheet that quantify the relationship or distance between the proposed electrical facilities and the proposed buildings.' Distances from transformers to parking/traffic areas are not dimensioned.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 requires that 'Equipment pads be located within 6 feet of parking/traffic areas for AE truck accessibility (unless otherwise specified by AE Design).' The applicant must either demonstrate that equipment pads are within 6 feet of parking/traffic areas (with dimensions), or provide written AE Design approval if different spacing is used.

perRunFindings.comment: Show drivable access routes from the nearest parking/traffic area to each transformer pad, with dimensions indicating the distance. If distance exceeds 6 feet, show the dedicated access route design.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) and Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) do not show drivable access routes to the transformer pad locations. Sheet 21 (Electrical Plan) shows transformers but does not indicate how Austin Energy trucks would access them for installation and maintenance. Without showing access routes, it cannot be verified that the transformer pads are accessible.
perRunFindings.reasoning: Per UCM § 1.10.4, pad-mounted transformers require drivable access routes for Austin Energy personnel and equipment. If a transformer is located more than 6 feet from an existing parking or traffic area, a dedicated access route must be provided and documented on the plans.

perRunFindings.comment: Distances from transformer pads to drivable surfaces not dimensionally verified on plans, and laydown curb specifications not shown. Provide dimensioned measurements confirming distances from each transformer pad to nearest drivable surface, and if distances exceed 6 feet, provide laydown curb details with minimum 12-foot width and adequate load capacity specifications.
applicableAreas: Transformer pads adjacent to driveways where distances exceed 6 feet
perRunFindings.observation: Examined Sheets 9 and 21. All four transformer pads are shown adjacent to paved driveways within approximately 6 feet based on visual scale (1" = 20'). However, specific measurement dimensions are not labeled on the plans. Sheet 9 shows one typical transformer pad labeled 'Transformer Pad (Typ.)' in a landscaped island between a sidewalk and drive aisle curb. No laydown curb specifications, dimensions, or details are shown on any sheet.
perRunFindings.reasoning: Code requires laydown curbs when transformer pads are not within 6 feet of drivable surface, with minimum 12-foot width and load capacity for transformer truck loads. The site plan shows transformers adjacent to driveways but does not explicitly measure the distances or confirm they are within 6 feet. Without clear dimensional verification of distances and explicit design details for any laydown curbs (including 12-foot minimum width and load capacity specifications), compliance cannot be determined.

comments.title: Transmission Structure Clearances to Proposed Buildings Not Documented
comments.comment: Proposed buildings and site features are not dimensioned against transmission structure locations referenced in the Sheet 3 general notes.
comments.issue: Sheet 3 Block 20 Electric Transmission Notes (16 items) specify active transmission facilities on or immediately adjacent to the site, including a 25-foot no-dig/no-grade zone around transmission structures, minimum clearances for aerial equipment and staging areas, road/driveway load requirements in easement areas, and prohibitions on structures within the transmission easement. Transmission pole and structure locations are not shown on Sheet 9 or Sheet 21, making it impossible to verify that proposed buildings and site features maintain required clearances from transmission infrastructure.
comments.sheets: General Notes (Sheet 3); Site Plan (Sheet 9); Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21)
comments.applicableArea: Proposed buildings (Buildings 1–8) and site features adjacent to transmission facilities on or immediately adjacent to the site
comments.resolution: Show transmission pole and structure locations on Sheet 9 (Site Plan) and Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan). Dimension clearances from proposed buildings and site features to transmission structures confirming the 25-foot no-dig/no-grade zone and all other restrictions listed in Sheet 3 Block 20 Electric Transmission Notes. Coordinate with Austin Energy Transmission C&M (Andrew Perez, 512-505-7153, per Sheet 3 Block 20) to confirm that building and site feature locations meet transmission facility clearance requirements and include written verification on the final plans.
comments.crossDepartmentNote: May involve coordination with Austin Energy Transmission C&M (contact: Andrew Perez, 512-505-7153 per Sheet 3 Block 20) to confirm compliance with transmission facility clearance requirements.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Low confidence (1/3 runs, unclear status) — verify whether transmission structures are present on/adjacent to the site and whether clearances are documented elsewhere in the submitted plans.

perRunFindings.comment: Clearance conflicts between proposed buildings and transmission facilities not documented or dimensioned. Coordinate with Austin Energy Transmission C&M (per Sheet 3 Block 20 note: contact Andrew Perez 512-505-7153) to confirm building locations maintain required clearances from transmission poles/structures. Add clearance dimensions to site and electrical plans showing compliance with UCM § 1.10.4 and transmission facility requirements (25 feet from transmission structures, proper staging area clearances, etc.). Include Austin Energy clearance verification documentation on final plans.
applicableAreas: proposed buildings and site features adjacent to transmission facilities
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 3 (General Notes) Block 20 contains detailed 'Electric Transmission Notes' with 16 items specifying clearance requirements and restrictions for transmission facilities on the property. These notes reference no digging/grading within 25 feet of transmission structures, minimum clearances from aerial equipment and staging areas, road/driveway load requirements for easement areas, and prohibitions on structures in transmission easement. However, Sheet 21 (Electrical Site Plan) and Sheet 9 (Site Plan) do not show clearance dimensions between the proposed buildings (Bldgs 1-8) and transmission structures or indicate how the 25-foot no-dig/no-grade clearance has been maintained around any transmission poles or structures. Vision analysis of Sheet 21 found transformer pads and buildings depicted but no clearance annotations or dimensions between buildings and transmission facilities. The site plan does not show transmission pole or structure locations, making it impossible to verify from the documents whether buildings and site features meet the required clearances.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 establishes minimum clearances from Austin Energy equipment. Sheet 3 Block 20 demonstrates that transmission facilities are present on/adjacent to the site, requiring compliance with transmission facility clearances (25 feet no-dig, 20 feet for aerial equipment, etc.). Sheet 21 does not show transmission structure locations or clearance dimensions between buildings and transmission infrastructure. Without documented verification that buildings and site features maintain required clearances from transmission facilities, compliance cannot be confirmed.

comments.title: Transformer Clearance Dimensions and Door Locations Not Annotated on Electrical Plan
comments.comment: Sheet 21 depicts transformer pad symbols only — no clearance dimension lines, operating door locations, or clearance zone callouts are shown for any of the four to five pad-mounted transformers.
comments.issue:
UCM § 1.10.4 requires that plans annotate all clearance dimensions for pad-mounted transformers and indicate door/control-side orientation, because clearance minimums vary by equipment side. The following are missing from Sheet 21 (and Sheet 9 where applicable):
- Clearance dimension lines from each pad to adjacent buildings, parking areas, driveways, fire escapes, windows, doors, and ventilating ducts (required minimums include: 10 ft for hot-stick use areas facing open space, 15 ft facing confined spaces, 5–12 ft from building walls depending on construction type, 20 ft from fire escapes, 3–5 ft on non-operating sides)
- Identification of the operating door/control side for each pad and direction of door swing
- Differentiated clearance zone callouts for operating vs. non-operating sides
- Written AE Design approval for any clearance reduction (UCM § 1.10.4 footnote 2 permits one 5-ft side reduced to 3 ft with written approval; standard AE requirements are 10–15 ft hot-stick area, 5 ft sides with operators, 3 ft other sides)
Note: runs identified either 4 or 5 transformer pads on Sheet 21; reviewer should confirm the actual count.
comments.sheets: Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21); Site Plan (Sheet 9)
comments.applicableArea: Four to five transformer pad locations on Sheet 21: west of Building 1, west of Building 2, south of Building 8, between Buildings 4–5, south of Building 6 (per run-1 of 15:EL-15.8); also described as 4 pads in other runs
comments.resolution: On Sheet 21, annotate each transformer pad with: (1) dimension lines showing minimum clearance distances from all four pad sides to adjacent features (buildings, parking, driveways, fire escapes, windows, doors, vents); (2) an arrow or label identifying which pad side contains the operating door and controls; (3) differentiated clearance zone callouts for the operating side vs. non-operating sides, referencing the specific UCM § 1.10.4 minimums for each side condition. If any proposed clearance falls below the UCM § 1.10.4 standard minimum for that side, submit written AE Design approval per footnote 2. Update Sheet 9 to be consistent with transformer locations and clearances depicted on Sheet 21.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Low confidence (1/3 runs each for component findings) — reviewer should confirm no clearance dimensions or door orientation markers are present on Sheet 21 or Sheet 9.

perRunFindings.comment: Transformer clearances per UCM § 1.10.4 are not shown on the plans. Annotate all transformer pad locations with minimum clearance dimensions showing: distance to nearest building, distance to parking/traffic areas, distance to fire escapes/stairs, distance to windows/doors/vents (if applicable), and verification that no structures overhang the pads. Use dimension lines and callouts to clearly demonstrate compliance with all applicable clearance requirements.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 shows 5 transformer pads marked as blue squares with leader lines and text labels 'Electrical Transformer Pad' and locations west of Bldg. 1, west of Bldg. 2, south of Bldg. 8, between Bldg. 4-5, and south of Bldg. 6. However, no clearance dimensions are annotated on the plan. No measurements are shown indicating distances from transformer pad edges to: adjacent buildings, parking areas, driveways, fire escapes, windows, doors, ventilation ducts, or other structures. Sheet 9 shows only one transformer marked as 'Transformer Pad (Typ.)' with no clearance dimensions indicated. The vision analysis confirmed that 'There are no specific measurements, depths, or clearances shown at the crossing points or along the routing paths on this plan view.'
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 specifies detailed clearance requirements for pad-mounted transformers including: 10 ft clearance to open area, 15 ft to confined spaces, 5 ft from removable fences, 3 ft from certain fence types, 20 ft from fire escapes, 5-12 ft from buildings depending on construction type, and no covering allowed above. Plans must show these clearances are met. Without dimensions and clearance annotations, it is impossible to verify compliance with these requirements. The plans do not demonstrate that clearances are adequate.

perRunFindings.comment: Provide detailed transformer pad location and clearance drawings showing all dimensions, setbacks from buildings, property lines, utilities, and landscaping per UCM § 1.10.4 standards. If any clearance reductions are proposed, provide written approval from AE Design per UCM § 1.10.4 footnote 2.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 shows four transformer pads but provides no clearance dimensions or specifications. Vision analysis indicated pads are positioned: (1) west of Bldg. 1, (2) west of Bldg. 8, (3) east of Bldg. 5, and (4) east of Bldg. 6. No measurements or setback distances shown. Standard AE requirements are 10-15 feet hot-stick area, 5 feet sides with operators, 3 feet other sides.

Without clearance dimensions shown on the plans and no AE approval of any non-standard configurations, cannot verify compliance. Need detailed transformer pad location drawings showing all clearances and dimensions relative to buildings, property lines, utilities, and landscaping.

perRunFindings.comment: Transformer clearance zones per UCM § 1.10.4 must be clearly shown on the electrical plan with dimension lines indicating minimum clearance distances from buildings, structures, obstacles, and access areas.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows transformer pad locations as simple rectangular symbols with no clearance dimensions, clearance zones, or buffer areas indicated around them. Vision analysis confirms: 'No clearance zones marked, No indication of dedicated electrical clearance zones, specific electrical maintenance access routes, or bollard locations protecting the electrical equipment.' Transformers are shown but with no notation of required clearance distances in any direction.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 specifies detailed clearance requirements for pad-mounted transformers including 10-ft clearance for hot-stick use areas adjacent to open areas or buildings, 15-ft clearance when facing confined spaces, 3-5 ft clearances from ventilated obstructions, 20-ft clearance from fire escapes, 5-12 ft clearance from building walls depending on material, and no covering above. These clearances must be shown on plans with dimensions and notations to document compliance. Without clearance zones depicted, review agencies cannot verify that the site design accommodates these requirements.

perRunFindings.comment: Transformer door location must be clearly indicated for each of the five pad-mounted transformers on Sheet 21. Use arrows, labels, or detailed callouts to show the side of each pad where the operating door is located, and indicate the direction of door swing. This is necessary to verify that clearances per UCM § 1.10.4 are adequate for equipment access.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 shows 5 transformer pads marked with blue square symbols and labeled 'Electrical Transformer Pad' at their locations, but no transformer door locations are indicated. No callouts, arrows, or detailed insets show which side of each pad contains the door opening, the direction the door swings, the clearance needed for door operation, or any operating access information. The vision analysis noted that transformers are marked only with their general location but no specific door information is provided.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 requires clear indication of transformer door locations because: (1) door location determines which side requires operating clearance, (2) door location affects required clearance dimensions (different clearances for different sides per § 1.10.4), and (3) door location must be known to verify sufficient space for door swing and equipment access. Without this information, clearances cannot be properly verified.

perRunFindings.comment: Show transformer pad door locations and control positions on the electrical plan, and indicate clearance zones appropriate to each side per UCM § 1.10.4 based on equipment orientation and adjacent features.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows four transformer pads as simple rectangular symbols with no indication of door locations, swing arcs, clearance zones, or operational access areas. Vision analysis confirms: 'There is no indication of door locations or designated clearance zones around the transformer pads.' The transformer pad symbols do not differentiate between different sides of the pad or indicate which side has the operating door and controls.
perRunFindings.reasoning: Per UCM § 1.10.4, the clearance requirements for pad-mounted transformers vary depending on the equipment side. Sides with operating controls/doors ('hot-stick use areas') require 10-15 ft clearance depending on whether they face open space or confined space. Sides without controls require 3-5 ft clearance. Showing the door location and control side is essential for proper site design to ensure the specified clearances are available on the correct sides of the equipment. Without this detail, compliance cannot be verified.

comments.title: Transformer Pad Drainage Design Missing from Grading Plan
comments.comment: Transformer pad locations are not identified on the Grading Plan, and no spot elevations or drainage flow arrows demonstrate that oil-filled equipment drainage is directed away from buildings.
comments.issue: UCM § 1.10.4 footnote 1 requires that grading and drainage around oil-filled pad-mounted equipment be designed to direct liquid flow away from buildings. Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) does not depict any transformer pad locations, provide spot elevations at or around the pads, or include drainage flow arrows demonstrating compliant flow direction relative to the electrical equipment. The general site contours shown on Sheet 11 (elevations ranging 672–690 ft; contour lines at 680 and 682 ft visible) do not substitute for pad-specific drainage callouts. The absence of transformer pads on the grading plan creates a disconnect between the electrical design (Sheet 21) and the drainage design, making it impossible to verify that drainage around these oil-filled transformers flows away from building foundations.
comments.sheets: Grading Plan (Sheet 11); Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21)
comments.applicableArea: All transformer pad locations (four pads shown on Sheet 21); drainage areas surrounding transformer pads
comments.resolution: On Sheet 11, add transformer pad location symbols cross-referenced to the pad designations on Sheet 21. For each pad, add: (1) spot elevations on all four sides of the pad; (2) drainage flow arrows demonstrating that surface water and any oil spill flow is directed away from transformer pads and away from building foundations. If general site grading achieves this condition without pad-specific grading, add a note on Sheet 11 citing specific spot elevations and confirming the drainage direction.

perRunFindings.comment: Transformer pad locations shown on Electrical Design Plan but drainage direction around pads is not indicated on either electrical or grading plans. Grading Plan does not depict transformer pads, creating no cross-reference showing how stormwater drains relative to oil-filled equipment. applicableAreas: grading and drainage areas around electrical equipment
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design) depicts 4 transformer pads but provides no specific drainage direction indicators, spot elevations, or grading notes showing how stormwater is directed around these pads. Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) does not show transformer pad locations at all - it only shows building footprints, storm drain routing in the drive aisles, retaining walls, and drainage easements. The transformer pads are not depicted on the grading plan, creating a disconnect between the electrical design and the drainage design. General contour lines pass through the site (elevations ranging 672-690 feet) but no specific micro-drainage detail is provided for the individual transformer pads. The electrical sheet's general site contours and the grading plan's drainage flow arrows do not specifically address how drainage is directed relative to the transformer pad locations. No notation on either sheet indicates that drainage around pad-mounted equipment (particularly oil-filled transformers) is designed to flow away from buildings.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 requires that grading and drainage around oil-filled pad-mounted equipment be directed away from buildings. The site plan materials show transformer locations (Sheet 21) and site grading/drainage (Sheet 11) separately without cross-reference or specific notation demonstrating compliance. The fact that transformer pads are not depicted on the grading plan means the grading design has not explicitly addressed drainage direction around these electrical facilities. Without specific drainage callouts, arrows, or elevations tied to the transformer pads showing drainage flow direction, it cannot be verified that the requirement for drainage to flow away from buildings is met. The absence of this specification in either the electrical or grading plans constitutes unclear compliance.

perRunFindings.comment: Grading/drainage direction around oil-filled pad-mounted equipment not designed or documented. Identify all transformer pad locations on Grading Plan. Show spot elevations for each transformer pad and surrounding terrain. Add drainage flow arrows demonstrating that grading slopes and surface water flow direct water away from transformer pads per UCM § 1.10.4. Provide drainage design calculations or notes confirming compliance.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 shows four transformer pad locations. Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) does not identify or label any transformer pads. No spot elevations, drainage flow arrows, or grading notes are shown around transformer pad locations on the Grading Plan. No elevation data is provided for the transformer pads themselves. The grading plan shows general site topography and contour lines (680, 682, etc.) but does not specifically address drainage direction or protection requirements around the electrical equipment.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 (footnote 1) requires that grading and drainage direction around oil-filled pad-mounted equipment be designed to flow away from buildings. The grading plan must identify transformer locations, show spot elevations for pads, and indicate drainage flow direction with arrows to confirm water is directed away from equipment. The absence of transformer pad identification and drainage notation on the Grading Plan prevents verification of compliance with drainage requirements. This is a critical oversight as improper drainage toward transformers can cause damage and environmental contamination.

perRunFindings.comment: Show transformer pad locations on the grading plan with spot elevations on all four sides of each pad, demonstrating that ground slopes direct drainage flow away from buildings and towards site drainage areas.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) shows site contours, retaining walls, and drainage features but does not indicate transformer pad locations or spot elevations around them. perRunFindings.reasoning: Per UCM § 1.10.4 Table 1.10.4 footnote 1, grading around oil-filled pad-mounted transformer equipment must direct liquid flow away from buildings. This is a critical safety and environmental requirement. The grading plan must show transformer locations with spot elevations on all sides of the pad demonstrating that slopes direct flow away from building foundations and towards site drainage. Without this detail, code compliance cannot be verified and environmental risks cannot be assessed.

comments.comment: The 39-sheet plan set does not include architectural elevation sheets demonstrating transformer pad clearances from windows, stairs, doors, and ventilating ducts as required by UCM § 1.10.4.

comments.title: Transformer Pad Locations Not Cross-Referenced Against Underground Parking Structure
comments.comment: The site includes 78 underground parking spaces, but no cross-reference between transformer pad locations and subsurface conditions confirms that no pads are situated over basement levels or the subgrade parking garage.

Without a plan or section overlaying transformer pad locations with the subsurface garage footprint, compliance with this prohibition cannot be verified.
comments.sheets: Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21); Site Plan (Sheet 9); Grading Plan (Sheet 11)
comments.applicableArea: Transformer pad locations adjacent to Buildings 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8 — relationship to 78-space underground parking garage

comments.title: Electric Conductor Clearance to Buildings Lacks AE Coordination Documentation
comments.comment: No clearance analysis or Austin Energy coordination documentation has been provided demonstrating that proposed buildings comply with required separation distances from existing electric transmission facilities and overhead electric conductors on the property.
comments.issue: UCM § 1.10.4 requires that clearance conflicts between existing electric conductors and proposed buildings be discussed with and resolved by Austin Energy Design prior to site plan approval. Sheet 3 documents 16 Electric Transmission Notes confirming transmission facilities exist on the property; Sheet 21 shows OHE (Overhead Electric) lines running along the southern and western property boundaries and right-of-way. Neither sheet provides clearance dimensions between proposed Buildings 1–8 and any conductors, nor is any Austin Energy Design approval letter, clearance determination, or coordination documentation submitted demonstrating design-phase conflict resolution. The transmission notes on Sheet 3 address pre-construction coordination requirements (e.g., grading near transmission facilities, safety meetings) but do not constitute design-phase conflict resolution per UCM § 1.10.4 and NESC standards.
comments.sheets: Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21); General Notes (Sheet 3); Site Plan (Sheet 9)
comments.applicableArea: Electrical transmission easement; proposed Buildings 1–8; overhead electric (OHE) lines along southern and western property boundaries/right-of-way
comments.resolution: Provide clearance dimensions between all proposed buildings (Buildings 1–8) and all existing electric transmission conductors and OHE lines on the Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21). Submit Austin Energy Design approval documentation (coordination letter or clearance determination) confirming that proposed building locations and heights comply with NESC and UCM § 1.10.4 clearance requirements.
comments.crossDepartmentNote: Resolution requires coordination with Austin Energy Design, which must evaluate and approve clearance compliance before this deficiency can be closed.

perRunFindings.comment: Clearance conflicts between existing transmission conductors and proposed buildings have not been discussed with and documented as resolved by Austin Energy Design. Provide clearance dimensions between all proposed buildings and transmission line conductors, and include Austin Energy Design approval documentation confirming that proposed building locations and heights comply with NESC and UCM § 1.10.4 clearance requirements.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 3 (General Notes) documents that transmission facilities and transmission easement exist on the property through 16 separate Electric Transmission Notes. Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows the proposed buildings (Buildings 1-8) and electrical infrastructure layout but does not depict or document any clearance dimensions between the proposed buildings and the existing transmission facilities. No distance measurements, clearance zones, or conflict identification are shown on the electrical site plan. Sheet 3 transmission notes require pre-construction grading coordination with Austin Energy (ET Note 2: 'Grading near electric transmission facilities must be coordinated with Austin Energy prior to commencement of grading') and mandate a safety meeting (ET Note 3). However, there is no documentation on the site plan sheets showing that clearance conflicts between the proposed buildings and transmission conductors have been identified and discussed with Austin Energy Design during the site plan phase. The coordination notes address pre-construction requirements, not design-phase conflict resolution.
perRunFindings.reasoning: EL-19.14 requires 'Clearance conflict between existing electric conductors and proposed buildings not discussed with and resolved by Austin Energy Design.' The grouping specifies checking 'Proximity of proposed buildings to electric lines; clearance dimensions; Austin Energy coordination documentation addressing conflicts.' Sheet 3 transmission notes indicate transmission facilities exist on site. Sheet 21 shows proposed buildings but without any documentation of clearance analysis or conflict resolution with transmission lines. The presence of transmission notes requiring pre-construction coordination does not constitute design-phase conflict resolution. Per UCM § 1.10.4 and the National Electric Safety Code (referenced in Sheet 3 ET Notes), clearance conflicts must be identified and resolved during design, not deferred to construction. No conflict analysis or Austin Energy Design approval letter addressing transmission clearances to proposed structures is visible in the application documents.

perRunFindings.comment: Coordinate with Austin Energy regarding clearance between existing overhead electric conductors (OHE lines shown on property perimeter) and proposed buildings. Obtain Austin Energy clearance determination addressing any potential conflicts and document resolution on the electrical site plan per UCM § 1.10.4.
applicableAreas: Existing overhead electric lines and proposed building locations
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows dashed lines labeled 'OHE' (Overhead Electric) running along the southern and western property boundaries/Right-of-Way. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) depicts all eight buildings positioned within the site interior. The proximity of proposed buildings to existing overhead electric conductors is evident from the plan layout. However, no clearance dimension analysis, conflict assessment, or documentation of Austin Energy clearance discussion is visible on either sheet or in the supplementary documents. Sheet 3 contains a note about 'Electric Transmission Clearances' but this is a general note, not a site-specific conflict analysis. No Austin Energy coordination documentation or clearance letter addressing specific conflicts is provided.
perRunFindings.reasoning: The checklist deficiency states 'Clearance conflict between existing electric conductors and proposed buildings not discussed with and resolved by Austin Energy Design.' The site plan clearly shows existing overhead electric infrastructure (OHE lines on the perimeter) and proposes buildings in proximity to these lines. The code requires that clearance issues be 'discussed with and resolved by Austin Energy Design.' The absence of any clearance analysis, conflict resolution documentation, or Austin Energy coordination letter indicates this requirement has not been met. While buildings may not physically encroach the conductors, the site plan does not demonstrate that clearance conflicts (if any exist) have been addressed through proper Austin Energy engineering evaluation.

comments.title: Transformer Pad Drivable Access Routes Not Shown on Plans
comments.comment: Drivable access routes for Austin Energy service trucks to reach each of the five pad-mounted transformers are not depicted on the Site Plan or Landscape Plan.
comments.issue: UCM § 1.10.4 requires transformer pads to be located within 6 feet of a drivable surface (parking or traffic area) to enable Austin Energy truck access for transformer replacement and repair. Sheet 21 shows five pad-mounted transformers and underground routing but provides no drivable access route markings or annotations. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) and Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) do not show transformer pad locations at all, making access verification impossible on those sheets.
comments.sheets: Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21); Site Plan (Sheet 9); Landscape Plan (Sheet 31)
comments.resolution: Show all five transformer pad locations on Sheet 9 (Site Plan) and Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan). On each sheet, use arrows, dashed lines, or clear notation identifying how Austin Energy service trucks can access each pad. Confirm each pad is within 6 feet of a drivable parking or traffic surface; where any pad exceeds this distance, provide a dedicated marked access route.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Low confidence (1/3 runs) — reviewer should verify transformer pad locations on Sheet 21 and their proximity to drivable surfaces on the site plan before requiring this correction.

perRunFindings.comment: Drivable access routes to all transformer pads must be shown on the Site Plan (Sheet 9) and Landscape Plan (Sheet 31). Use arrows, dashed lines, or other clear notation to identify how Austin Energy trucks can access each transformer pad. Ensure each pad is located within 6 feet of a drivable surface (parking or traffic area) per UCM § 1.10.4, or provide marked dedicated access routes.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 shows 5 pad-mounted transformers and underground electric routing, but shows no drivable access route explicitly marked or labeled. The site plan (Sheet 9) and landscape plan (Sheet 31) do not show transformer pad locations at all, making it impossible to verify access routes on those sheets. UCM § 1.10.4 requires that transformer pads be located within 6 feet of parking/traffic areas for Austin Energy truck accessibility, which implies access routes must be shown. comments.title: Vault Easement Near Building 8 — Niche Equipment Classification Unclear
comments.comment: A 'Vault Easement' encompassing an electrical transformer pad is shown adjacent to Building 8 on the plans, but it is unclear whether this constitutes niche equipment subject to UCM § 1.10.4 design requirements.
comments.issue: UCM § 1.10.4 imposes specific design requirements for niche equipment — underground chambers accessible only from outside the building, with a minimum 35-foot interior vertical clearance, 3-hour fire-rated walls, and exterior-only accessibility. The plans show a 'Vault Easement' adjacent to Building 8 encompassing an electrical transformer pad (visible on Sheets 21 and 11) but do not designate this as niche equipment, nor do they provide detail drawings showing entrance configuration, interior clearances, or fire ratings. Without this clarification, it cannot be determined whether UCM § 1.10.4 niche-specific requirements apply.

comments.resolution: Clarify on the plans whether the Vault Easement adjacent to Building 8 is (1) a routine transformer access vault not subject to niche equipment requirements, or (2) niche equipment as defined by UCM § 1.10.4. If niche equipment, provide detail drawings demonstrating compliance with UCM § 1.10.4, including entrance configuration, minimum 35-foot interior vertical clearance, 3-hour fire-rated walls, and accessibility from outside the building only.

The grading plan (Sheet 11) shows this same 'Vault Easement' as a dashed rectangle near Building 8. The Downtown Network Area is generally defined as the downtown core and close-in neighborhoods; South Lamar is typically outside this boundary. However, the term 'Vault Easement' and its location 'adjacent to Building 8 and encompassing an Electrical Transformer Pad' requires clarification. A 'vault' could indicate either: (1) a standard transformer access vault (which is merely an enclosure, not niche equipment), or (2) actual niche equipment as defined by UCM § 1.10.4 (an underground chamber accessible only from outside the building, with 35-foot minimum vertical clearance, 3-hour fire walls). The plans do NOT explicitly designate this as 'niche equipment' or provide the detailed drawings (entrance configuration, interior clearances, fire-rating, accessibility) required by UCM § 1.10.4. Without such designation and details, compliance with niche-specific requirements cannot be verified, and it is unclear whether this item applies.

comments.title: Electric Service Loop System Requirement Not Established by ESPA
comments.comment: No Electric Service Planning Application (ESPA) approval documentation has been submitted to confirm whether an Austin Energy loop system is required for this site.
comments.issue: A loop system is a specialized Austin Energy service configuration required only in certain network conditions; its applicability is established through the ESPA process. Sheet 21 shows proposed underground electric routing from transformers to pull boxes and building meters but does not depict a loop system design, and no ESPA approval letter or Austin Energy correspondence confirming or excluding a loop system requirement has been submitted. Without the ESPA determination, the applicability of this requirement cannot be assessed.
comments.resolution: Submit Austin Energy ESPA approval documentation confirming whether a loop system is required for this site. If a loop system is required, show the complete loop system design on Sheet 21 and all other applicable plan sheets per UCM § 1.10.4. If a loop system is not required, the ESPA letter confirming this determination resolves the deficiency.
